results.text: Ananta, what is small case? Like, you know, in India, there is an operating web platform named Smallcase, right? And like, how does they operate and how does they pick stocks and what's their criteria and selection of their stocks? And how are they sizing people for alternatives every week or so? What is their like working structure there?
results.answer: Sir, Smallcase is a platform where SEBI-registered advisers and asset managers publish ready-made baskets of up to about 50 stocks or ETFs built around a theme or rule (momentum, quality, dividends, a sector). You buy the whole basket in one click through your own broker, so the shares sit in your own demat account. Smallcase doesn't pick the stocks: each manager sets their own selection rules and fixed percentage weights, and the minimum investment is whatever it takes to buy at least one share of every stock at those weights. Managers rebalance on their own schedule, usually monthly or quarterly rather than weekly as far as I know; you get a notice and choose whether to apply it, paying broker charges plus the manager's fee. Ananta hasn't tested any smallcase's strategy, so I can't say whether one beats a plain Nifty index fund.

results.text: Ananta, apart from moving averages, how well is momentum is good for us? How are we watching it as a buying indicator or selling indicator? And what other main indicators are the most influential indicators according to you in the market? Which one is worth waiting for watching out for volume, momentum? What is your catch on them?
results.answer: Sir, momentum in the months-long sense (3 to 12 months of relative strength) is the nearest thing to a buy indicator. That test came close to the strict pass mark, so a 20-session paper trial is running, but nothing trades from it yet. RSI (a 0-100 stretch gauge) works only as a "don't chase" filter: stocks bought with RSI over 70 earned about 1.5-2% less over the next 20 sessions than the rest, and buying under 30 earned about 2% more, though that held up less cleanly once the exits were varied. MACD crossovers failed the test, and volume is not a signal either: breakouts on heavy volume fell back less in the first week but earned less over the next 20 sessions. The most useful tested warning is distance from the 50-day average: uptrend stocks bought 8-15% above it earned about 1-1.5% less over 20 sessions, so these indicators tell you what to avoid, not what to buy.

results.text: Okay. What would be the best buy signal in the market? Like, see, let's say if you want to buy a Bank Nifty option tomorrow, at what situation will you buy it?
results.answer: Sir, Ananta has found no single best buy signal, and none of the standard indicators it tested works as one. Its Bank Nifty rule looks at the gap, the trend, India VIX, the US close, the first minutes' move and breadth at 09:15, 09:30, 09:45 and 10:15 IST (10:45 to 11:45 pm Toronto). It buys one lot only if the predicted move, after costs of about 33 points, is above zero and above half its own uncertainty, and otherwise it waits. A call needs the index to rise by more than the option's daily time-value melt plus costs, so a gap up that holds or a trend that builds in the first hour helps and a choppy range bleeds, and no trade is the usual answer.

results.text: Okay Ananta. So when you are buying a stock, is there any deep analysis that you are doing, the fundamentals and the results and the competitors? Is that some sort of research? Is that something that is going with us? How are you just picking a stock? What's your criteria?
results.answer: Sir, no: Ananta does not do deep company research when it picks a stock. It screens on price and volume only, such as a breakout above a one-month high on heavy volume, a strong stock resting at its one-month average, or a stock sold too hard. It also applies the tested don't-chase filters, and the random comparison picks are the yardstick. Results are on file only for 2018-2023 and there are no analyst estimates or peer comparisons, so a view on fundamentals or competitors is not something it has, and results days are just flagged as risk.

results.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
results.answer: Sir, an idea climbs a fixed staircase, and no step is skipped. A draft waits for your yes; then its test is written down before it runs and it is tested on 2000-2023 at a the strict pass mark; then it runs as a paper book on 20 live sessions. Only if it beats random picks and the market average on 10 separate sessions after costs, passes the check that no future data leaked in, and you say yes again is it admitted, and only then may the allocated paper capital use it. After that comes the final real-money gate, which needs your yes too, and nothing is placed from chat.
